AUTH-9262.remediation: sudo apt install libpam-pwquality  # then add 'minlen=12 ucredit=-1 lcredit=-1 dcredit=-1' to /etc/pam.d/common-password
AUTH-9262.explanation: Prevents users from choosing weak, easily-guessable passwords, reducing the risk of brute-force or credential-stuffing compromise.

AUTH-9286.explanation: Limits how long a compromised password stays valid and encourages regular rotation, reducing long-term credential exposure.

AUTH-9328.explanation: A stricter umask prevents newly created files from being readable/writable by other local users by default, reducing accidental data exposure.

AUTH-9228.explanation: Detects inconsistencies or corruption in the password database that could indicate tampering or misconfiguration.

AUTH-9230.remediation: Configure password hashing rounds (e.g. SHA_CRYPT_MIN_ROUNDS / SHA_CRYPT_MAX_ROUNDS) in /etc/login.defs
AUTH-9230.explanation: Increases the computational cost of cracking stolen password hashes.

ACCT-9628.remediation: sudo apt install auditd audispd-plugins && sudo systemctl enable --now auditd
ACCT-9628.explanation: Provides detailed audit trails of security-relevant system calls and events, which is critical for detecting and investigating intrusions.

ACCT-9622.remediation: sudo apt install acct && sudo systemctl enable --now acct 2>/dev/null || sudo touch /var/log/wtmp
ACCT-9622.explanation: Enables historical tracking of user logins/commands, useful for forensic analysis after an incident.

ACCT-9626.remediation: sudo apt install sysstat && sudo systemctl enable --now sysstat
ACCT-9626.explanation: Collects historical system resource usage, useful for spotting anomalies and forensic analysis after an incident.

HRDN-7230.remediation: sudo apt install rkhunter chkrootkit clamav && sudo rkhunter --update && sudo rkhunter --propupd
HRDN-7230.explanation: Detects rootkits, trojans, and other malicious software that could otherwise go unnoticed on the system.

FINT-4350.remediation: sudo apt install aide && sudo aideinit
FINT-4350.explanation: Alerts you when critical system files are modified unexpectedly, which is often a sign of compromise.

KRNL-6000.remediation: Create /etc/sysctl.d/99-hardening.conf with keys such as kernel.kptr_restrict=2, kernel.dmesg_restrict=1, fs.suid_dumpable=0, net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=1, then run: sudo sysctl --system
KRNL-6000.explanation: These kernel-level settings shrink the attack surface for kernel-pointer leaks, kernel exploits, and network spoofing/redirect attacks.

KRNL-5820.explanation: Disables core dumps, preventing sensitive memory contents from being written to disk after a crash.

BOOT-5122.impact: Usability — adds password prompt for boot edits
BOOT-5122.remediation: grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2  # copy hash, then add set superusers="admin" and password_pbkdf2 admin <hash> to /etc/grub.d/40_custom, then: sudo update-grub
BOOT-5122.explanation: Prevents anyone with physical/console access from altering boot parameters or booting into single-user/root mode without authentication.

BOOT-5264.remediation: Run: systemd-analyze security SERVICE  for each running service and tighten sandboxing directives
BOOT-5264.explanation: Identifies systemd services that could be further sandboxed to limit their capabilities if compromised.

BANN-7126.remediation: printf 'Authorized users only. All activity may be monitored.\n' | sudo tee /etc/issue
BANN-7126.explanation: Establishes a documented legal basis for prosecuting unauthorized access and clarifies that activity may be monitored.

BANN-7130.remediation: printf 'Authorized users only. All activity may be monitored.\n' | sudo tee /etc/issue.net
BANN-7130.explanation: Establishes a documented legal basis for prosecuting unauthorized network access and clarifies that activity may be monitored.

USB-1000.explanation: Reduces the risk of data exfiltration or malware introduction via removable USB storage devices.

LOGG-2154.impact: None locally — needs external log server
LOGG-2154.remediation: echo '*.* @@your-log-server:514' | sudo tee /etc/rsyslog.d/90-remote.conf && sudo systemctl restart rsyslog
LOGG-2154.explanation: Protects log integrity by storing copies off-host, so an attacker who compromises the system can't erase evidence of their activity.

LOGG-2190.remediation: sudo lsof +L1   # identify processes; then restart the owning app/process (e.g. killall brave) or reboot
LOGG-2190.explanation: Reclaims disk space held by processes still referencing deleted files; mostly a housekeeping item rather than a security concern.

PKGS-7370.remediation: sudo apt install debsums && sudo debsums -c
PKGS-7370.explanation: Verifies installed package files against known-good checksums, helping detect tampering.

PKGS-7394.explanation: Helps track which installed packages have newer versions available, supporting patch management.

PKGS-7398.explanation: Helps you proactively identify installed packages with known, unpatched vulnerabilities (CVEs).

PKGS-7420.impact: Usability — auto-updates can disrupt running services
PKGS-7420.remediation: sudo apt install unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades
PKGS-7420.explanation: Ensures security patches are applied promptly without relying on manual intervention, reducing the window of exposure to known exploits.

HRDN-7222.impact: Usability — breaks compiling for non-root/dev users
HRDN-7222.remediation: sudo chmod 750 /usr/bin/gcc /usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc-13 /usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-as && sudo chgrp devs /usr/bin/gcc  # add trusted users to 'devs' group
HRDN-7222.explanation: Makes it harder for an attacker or malware with limited/non-root access to compile and run custom exploit code on the system.

FILE-6310.remediation: No simple CLI fix — requires repartitioning/reinstall (e.g. via LVM resize or fresh install with separate mount points)
FILE-6310.explanation: Separate partitions contain the impact of a filled disk, runaway logs, or a compromised service, preventing it from crashing the whole system.

FILE-7524.remediation: Review file permissions flagged in the Lynis log and tighten with chmod as appropriate
FILE-7524.explanation: Overly permissive file permissions can allow unauthorized local users to read or modify sensitive files.

PROC-3612.remediation: ps aux | grep -i defunct   # investigate and, if needed, restart the parent process
PROC-3612.explanation: Zombie/dead processes can indicate a misbehaving parent process and, in rare cases, resource exhaustion.

NAME-4028.remediation: Review /etc/resolv.conf and DNS search domain configuration
NAME-4028.explanation: Ensures DNS resolution is configured as expected and not silently misconfigured or hijacked.

NETW-3200.remediation: echo 'install dccp /bin/true' | sudo tee -a /etc/modprobe.d/disable-uncommon-protocols.conf  # repeat for sctp, rds, tipc as needed
NETW-3200.explanation: Uncommon network protocols increase kernel attack surface if they're loaded but never actually used.

PRNT-2307.impact: Usability — may restrict local CUPS admin access
PRNT-2307.remediation: Review /etc/cups/cupsd.conf access controls for the admin/config endpoints
PRNT-2307.explanation: Restricting CUPS configuration access reduces the risk of unauthorized printer/service reconfiguration.

MACF-6208.explanation: Confirms AppArmor profiles are loaded and enforcing, which contains what a compromised process can do.

TOOL-5002.remediation: Consider installing a configuration management tool (e.g. Ansible) if managing multiple systems
TOOL-5002.explanation: Automation tooling improves consistency and auditability of system configuration changes over time.
